facts.fact: The board of the national regulator ARN-TIC put the draft Electronic Transactions Law (covering electronic communications and transactions, trust services and e-government) out for public consultation, with responses due by 28 May 2026; the notice's date is not given, so the published date 2026-05-08 is used.

facts.fact: The document is the 112-article Projecto de Lei das Transacções Electrónicas de 2025 (bill number and publication date left blank, masthead dated 6 September 2025), which would give data messages, electronic records, contracts and electronic signatures legal effect, license trust-service providers and set e-commerce consumer rules, and which enters into force only on a date the Minister designates; ARN put this revised text to public consultation, dated here by the document's published date 2026-05-08.

facts.fact: The Agencia de Noticias da Guine reports that Guinea-Bissau's Council of Ministers examined the proposed Electronic Transactions Law on 17 November 2026, which its communique says aims to modernise the legal framework for electronic operations; no adoption is stated.

facts.fact: Guinea-Bissau's Council of Ministers approved, with amendments, a bill on Electronic Transactions on 24 November 2026, to set the legal framework for operations and transactions by electronic means.
